title: THE BURNT OFFERING, PIECE BY PIECE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he slaughtered the burnt offering. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against the sides of the altar. They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, including the head, and he burned them on the altar." - Lev 9:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Piece by piece. His sons handed the offering to him one section at a time, and he placed each piece on the fire.

There is no rushing this. It is slow, deliberate, physical work — and it makes a picture worth holding on to.

Consecration usually happens piece by piece. Very few people surrender everything to God in a single dramatic moment. Most of us hand things over gradually: this relationship this year, this ambition the next, this fear a decade later. God takes what we bring, piece by piece.

That is not failure. It is how growth normally works. Paul described himself as still pressing on toward the goal, not having yet arrived (Phil 3:12-14). He is confident that God who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion (Phil 1:6) — carry it on, over time.

If you feel frustrated that you have not surrendered everything at once, take heart. The offering went onto the altar in pieces, and the whole thing still ascended to God.

What is the next piece?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is the next piece of my life God is asking me to hand over?
2. Am I discouraged by slow growth when God is patiently working?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You receive my life piece by piece. Here is the next piece — take it. Amen.
